name: Ofcom Planned Network Deployments 2026
fact: Ofcom's 13 May 2026 report uses operator plans as of January 2026 and projects full-fibre/gigabit-capable coverage to January 2029, separating all plans from High Confidence plans.
gate: Planned deployment is not live serviceability at a parcel; even High Confidence plans require address-level availability verification before scoring.

name: Ofcom Planned Network Deployment hub
fact: Ofcom states its planned-network-deployment reports supplement Connected Nations and are not comprehensive or definitive coverage statements.
gate: Use forward-looking data as context only; never promote a parcel from a forecast without current address-level evidence.

name: Ofcom communications infrastructure reports index
fact: The Ofcom index was updated 27 May 2026 and links Spring 2026 current coverage plus Planned Network Deployments 2026.
gate: Report-index presence is discovery evidence, not site coverage.

name: Connected Nations Spring 2026
fact: Ofcom reports January 2026 UK residential full-fibre availability at 82% and gigabit-capable availability at 89%; mobile figures use operator signal predictions.
gate: National coverage percentages and predicted mobile coverage must not be transferred to a target parcel or address.

name: Ofcom Map Your Mobile million-user update
fact: Ofcom's 29 May 2026 update says Map Your Mobile combines crowdsourced Opensignal experience with predictive information from mobile networks.
gate: Consumer checker evidence is useful screening but is not a guaranteed engineering signal survey or development connectivity commitment.

name: Ofcom Map Your Mobile checker
fact: The checker displays local predicted 4G/5G coverage plus postcode-district performance information and warns buildings, trees and walls can affect service.
gate: Checker coverage does not guarantee indoor/outdoor service at an exact building footprint or future development.

name: Ofcom Map Your Mobile coverage checker update
fact: Ofcom states no signal-strength threshold can guarantee coverage 100% of the time and predicted coverage cannot be 100% accurate.
gate: Never convert predicted signal into certain service availability; exact site testing or operator evidence remains required.

name: NPPF chapter 10 communications infrastructure
fact: NPPF chapter 10 says planning should support electronic communications networks and prioritise full-fibre connections to existing and new development.
gate: National policy support does not prove a network operator will serve a specific parcel or that infrastructure is already live.

name: GOV.UK resources for communications network providers
fact: Government guidance stresses early cooperation between network providers, developers and local authorities, including access agreements and street works.
gate: Early engagement and deployment guidance are process evidence, not a completed wayleave, street-works permission or live connection.

name: Revised Telecommunications Security Code of Practice 2026
fact: Version 1.1 of the revised Telecommunications Security Code of Practice was issued 14 July 2026 for large and medium public telecoms providers.
gate: Provider security compliance context is separate from physical network coverage, serviceability and parcel readiness.

name: BDUK Project Gigabit monthly contract progress collection
fact: BDUK publishes monthly updates of premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit; the collection was updated 20 July 2026.
gate: Monthly management information is programme-level evidence and does not establish address-level serviceability.

name: Project Gigabit July 2026 contract progress
fact: BDUK's July release is a snapshot held on 16 July 2026 and explicitly warns of variable lag between contract delivery and data ingestion and says figures should not assess milestone compliance.
gate: Built-premises counts are not proof a target address is orderable and must not be used to infer contractual milestone completion.

name: Project Gigabit June 2026 contract progress
fact: The June 2026 table reports contracted and built premises by supplier/contract and is management information rather than an address-level availability checker.
gate: Contract-level built totals cannot be assigned to an individual parcel or postcode.

name: Project Gigabit May 2026 contract progress
fact: BDUK's May 2026 release warns that some reported built-premises counts fell because supplier data was resubmitted and revised.
gate: Treat management counts as revisable; never use a single monthly count as immutable parcel evidence.

name: Project Gigabit April 2026 contract progress
fact: The April 2026 release reports contract-level contracted/built premises and notes numbers are rounded.
gate: Rounded programme totals do not identify exact premises passed or order-ready addresses.

name: Project Gigabit March 2026 contract progress
fact: The March 2026 release records contract-level delivery with an explicit management-information methodology and rounding controls.
gate: Do not treat monthly contract totals as exact address coverage or a service order state.

name: Project Gigabit February 2026 contract progress
fact: The February 2026 release provides programme management counts across multiple Project Gigabit contracts.
gate: Historical monthly snapshots must be superseded by the newest official release for current programme context.

name: Project Gigabit January 2026 contract progress
fact: The January 2026 release is an earlier contract-level delivery snapshot in BDUK's monthly series.
gate: Use as historical trend context only; it cannot override later revisions or current address checks.

name: Project Gigabit contracts collection
fact: BDUK's collection lists local, regional and cross-regional Project Gigabit contracts and their current guidance pages.
gate: Contract listing is not proof any individual premises remains in scope or is already serviceable.

name: Project Gigabit Openreach framework
fact: The Openreach framework covers hard-to-reach premises and says preparatory planning/build work occurs before residents and businesses can request a connection from a service provider.
gate: Contract scope or completed civil build is not automatically an orderable retail broadband service at a target address.

name: Project Gigabit Cambridgeshire contract
fact: In May 2026 the Cambridgeshire contract was redesigned to around 35,000 premises because commercial rollout and market conditions changed.
gate: Original contract scope is superseded; use latest contract/address checker evidence and never assume an earlier listed premises remains in scope.
